      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "# 1. IDENTITY MATRICES & STRUCTURED ARRAYS/CLUSTERS\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "class IdentityMatrixGenerator:\n",
      "    \"\"\"Generates identity and scaled identity matrices for alignment, normalization and projection\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def generate_identity(size: int) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Standard identity matrix I(n)\"\"\"\n",
      "        return np.eye(size, dtype=np.float64)\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def scaled_identity(size: int, scale: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Scaled identity: s * I(n)\"\"\"\n",
      "        return scale * np.eye(size, dtype=np.float64)\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def block_identity(blocks: List[int]) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Block diagonal identity matrix for clustered data\"\"\"\n",
      "        return np.block([[np.eye(n) if i == j else np.zeros((n, m))\n",
      "                                for j, m in enumerate(blocks)] for i, n in enumerate(blocks)])\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def identity_projection(mat: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Project matrix onto identity subspace\"\"\"\n",
      "        n = mat.shape[0]\n",
      "        trace_val = np.trace(mat) / n\n",
      "        return trace_val * np.eye(n, dtype=np.float64)\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def orthogonalize_with_identity(mat: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Stabilize matrix using identity regularization\"\"\"\n",
      "        n = mat.shape[0]\n",
      "        reg = 1e-6 * np.eye(n)\n",
      "        return mat + reg\n",
      "\n",
      "class ArrayClusterManager:\n",
      "    \"\"\"Manages distributed arrays and clusters optimized for Edge AI and WebGPU\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    def __init__(self, total_arrays: int = 1500, base_shape: Tuple[int, int] = (4, 10), clusters: int = 8):\n",
      "        self.total_arrays = total_arrays\n",
      "        self.base_shape = base_shape\n",
      "        self.cluster_count = clusters\n",
      "        self.seed = 12345\n",
      "        np.random.seed(self.seed)\n",
      "\n",
      "    def generate_base_arrays(self) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Generate normalized base arrays\"\"\"\n",
      "        data = np.random.normal(loc=0.75, scale=0.08, size=(self.total_arrays, *self.base_shape))\n",
      "        return np.clip(data, 0.05, 0.995)\n",
      "\n",
      "    def split_into_clusters(self, data: np.ndarray) -> Dict[int, np.ndarray]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Distribute data across clusters for parallel processing\"\"\"\n",
      "        return {i: part for i, part in enumerate(np.array_split(data, self.cluster_count))}\n",
      "\n",
      "    def cluster_metadata(self, clusters: Dict[int, np.ndarray]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Generate metadata per cluster\"\"\"\n",
      "        meta = []\n",
      "        for cid, arr in clusters.items():\n",
      "            meta.append({\n",
      "                \"cluster_id\": cid,\n",
      "                \"shape\": arr.shape,\n",
      "                \"mean\": round(np.mean(arr), 6),\n",
      "                \"std\": round(np.std(arr), 6),\n",
      "                \"norm\": round(norm(arr, 'fro'), 6),\n",
      "                \"webgpu_ready\": USE_WEBGPU\n",
      "            })\n",
      "        return meta\n",
      "\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "# 2. FAST IONIC & MAGNETIC INFERENCE\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "class FastFieldInference:\n",
      "    \"\"\"Ultra-fast computation of ionic and magnetic fields optimized for Edge AI\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def ionic_field_distribution(mat: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Charge gradient and ionic current density\"\"\"\n",
      "        grad_x = np.gradient(mat, axis=1)\n",
      "        grad_y = np.gradient(mat, axis=0)\n",
      "        div = grad_x + grad_y\n",
      "        norm = np.max(np.abs(div)) + 1e-12\n",
      "        return np.clip(div / norm, -1.0, 1.0)\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def magnetic_flux_vector(mat: np.ndarray, mu_r: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Magnetic flux density using Biot-Savart approximation\"\"\"\n",
      "        current = FastFieldInference.ionic_field_distribution(mat)\n",
      "        r = np.sqrt(np.arange(mat.shape[1])**2 + 1e-12)\n",
      "        flux = (MU0 * mu_r / (2 * PI * r[None, :])) * current\n",
      "        return np.clip(flux / (np.max(np.abs(flux)) + 1e-12), -1.0, 1.0)\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def combined_field_inference(mat: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Single-step fast inference for Edge deployment\"\"\"\n",
      "        E_ionic = FastFieldInference.ionic_field_distribution(mat)\n",
      "        B_magnetic = FastFieldInference.magnetic_flux_vector(mat)\n",
      "        energy_density = 0.5 * (EPS0 * np.sum(E_ionic**2) + np.sum(B_magnetic**2) / MU0)\n",
      "        return {\n",
      "            \"ionic_field\": E_ionic.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"magnetic_field\": B_magnetic.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"ionic_strength\": round(np.linalg.norm(E_ionic), 6),\n",
      "            \"magnetic_flux\": round(np.linalg.norm(B_magnetic), 6),\n",
      "            \"field_energy_density\": round(energy_density, 12)\n",
      "        }\n",
      "\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "# 3. RELATIVISTIC ACCELERATION & VIOLET PHOTONICS\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "class RelativisticPhysics:\n",
      "    \"\"\"Einstein equivalence, particle acceleration, and Milky Way natural accelerator\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def lorentz_factor(v: Any) -> Any:\n",
      "        \"\"\"γ = 1 / sqrt(1 - v²/c²)\"\"\"\n",
      "        # Ensure v is a NumPy array for element-wise operations\n",
      "        v_np = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Calculate (v/C)^2\n",
      "        v_ratio_sq = (v_np / C)**2\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Term under the square root: 1 - (v/C)^2\n",
      "        # Clamp to a very small positive number to prevent sqrt of negative due to float precision\n",
      "        term_under_sqrt = np.maximum(1.0 - v_ratio_sq, 1e-15)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Calculate gamma for values where v < C\n",
      "        gamma_computed = 1.0 / np.sqrt(term_under_sqrt)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Apply the condition: if v >= C, return 1e12. Otherwise, use the computed value.\n",
      "        gamma_result = np.where(v_np >= C, 1e12, gamma_computed)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # If the original input was a scalar, return a scalar\n",
      "        if np.isscalar(v):\n",
      "            return gamma_result.item()\n",
      "        return gamma_result\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def einstein_energy_mass_equivalence(mass: float, velocity: float) -> Dict[str, float]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Total energy: E = γ m c²\"\"\"\n",
      "        gamma = RelativisticPhysics.lorentz_factor(velocity)\n",
      "        rest_energy = mass * C**2\n",
      "        total_energy = gamma * rest_energy\n",
      "        kinetic_energy = total_energy - rest_energy\n",
      "        return {\n",
      "            \"gamma\": round(gamma, 8),\n",
      "            \"rest_energy_J\": round(rest_energy, 12),\n",
      "            \"total_energy_J\": round(total_energy, 12),\n",
      "            \"kinetic_energy_J\": round(kinetic_energy, 12)\n",
      "        }\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def violet_photonic_acceleration(intensity: float, wavelength: float = 400e-9) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Acceleration using violet light radiation pressure\"\"\"\n",
      "        photon_energy = H * C / wavelength\n",
      "        photon_momentum = H / wavelength\n",
      "        flux = intensity / photon_energy\n",
      "        acceleration = (flux * photon_momentum) / M_E\n",
      "        gamma = RelativisticPhysics.lorentz_factor(np.sqrt(2 * acceleration * 1.0))\n",
      "        return {\n",
      "            \"wavelength_nm\": round(wavelength * 1e9, 2),\n",
      "            \"photon_energy_eV\": round(photon_energy / Q_E, 6),\n",
      "            \"acceleration_m_s2\": round(acceleration, 6),\n",
      "            \"lorentz_gamma\": round(gamma, 8),\n",
      "            \"effective_speed_m_s\": round(min(np.sqrt(2 * acceleration * 1.0), C), 2)\n",
      "        }\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def milky_way_natural_accelerator(charge: float = Q_E, mass: float = M_E) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Relativistic acceleration by galactic magnetic field — natural particle accelerator\"\"\"\n",
      "        # Gyroradius: r = γ m v / (q B)\n",
      "        # Energy gain over galactic scales\n",
      "        gamma_max = 1e7\n",
      "        energy_max = gamma_max * mass * C**2\n",
      "        speed = C * np.sqrt(1 - 1 / gamma_max**2)\n",
      "        gyroradius = gamma_max * mass * speed / (charge * B_GALACTIC)\n",
      "        return {\n",
      "            \"galactic_field_T\": B_GALACTIC,\n",
      "            \"max_lorentz_gamma\": gamma_max,\n",
      "            \"max_energy_eV\": round(energy_max / Q_E, 2),\n",
      "            \"gyroradius_ly\": round(gyroradius / 9.461e15, 4),\n",
      "            \"speed_ratio_c\": round(speed / C, 8)\n",
      "        }\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def particle_wave_duality(energy: float) -> Dict[str, float]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"De Broglie relations — equivalence between particle and wave properties\"\"\"\n",
      "        momentum = np.sqrt((energy / C)**2 - (M_E * C)**2) if energy > M_E * C**2 else np.sqrt(2 * M_E * energy)\n",
      "        wavelength = H / (momentum + 1e-36)\n",
      "        frequency = energy / H\n",
      "        return {\n",
      "            \"momentum_kg_m_s\": round(momentum, 36),\n",
      "            \"wavelength_m\": round(wavelength, 36),\n",
      "            \"frequency_Hz\": round(frequency, 12),\n",
      "            \"wave_number\": round(2 * PI / wavelength, 12)\n",
      "        }\n",
      "\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "# 4. PROCEDURAL DEEP LEARNING — 300+ LINES OF COMPLEX TRANSFORMS\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "class ProceduralDeepLearning:\n",
      "    \"\"\"WebGPU/Edge optimized procedural DL with relativistic and field features\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    def __init__(self, use_webgpu: bool = USE_WEBGPU):\n",
      "        self.use_webgpu = use_webgpu\n",
      "        self.identity_reg = IdentityMatrixGenerator()\n",
      "        self.weights = {}\n",
      "        self.biases = {}\n",
      "        self.seed = 98765\n",
      "        np.random.seed(self.seed)\n",
      "\n",
      "    def init_layer_weights(self, input_dim: int, output_dim: int, layer_id: str) -> None:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Initialize weights with identity stabilization\"\"\"\n",
      "        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (input_dim + output_dim))\n",
      "        w = np.random.normal(0.0, scale, (output_dim, input_dim))\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Generate a square identity matrix based on the minimum dimension\n",
      "        reg_square = self.identity_reg.generate_identity(min(input_dim, output_dim))\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Create a zero matrix of the same shape as w (output_dim, input_dim)\n",
      "        reg_expanded = np.zeros_like(w, dtype=w.dtype)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Embed the square identity matrix into the top-left corner of reg_expanded\n",
      "        rows_to_copy = reg_square.shape[0]\n",
      "        cols_to_copy = reg_square.shape[1]\n",
      "        reg_expanded[:rows_to_copy, :cols_to_copy] = reg_square\n",
      "\n",
      "        self.weights[layer_id] = w + 0.01 * reg_expanded # Apply the regularization factor\n",
      "        self.biases[layer_id] = np.zeros((output_dim, 1))\n",
      "\n",
      "    def irrational_transform(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Complex non-linear mapping using fundamental constants\"\"\"\n",
      "        return (\n",
      "            x * PI +\n",
      "            np.sin(x * E) +\n",
      "            np.cos(x * PHI) +\n",
      "            np.tanh(x * SQRT2) +\n",
      "            np.sinh(x * SQRT3) +\n",
      "            np.exp(x * ALPHA) -\n",
      "            np.log(np.abs(x) + E)\n",
      "        ) / 6.0\n",
      "\n",
      "    def relativistic_activation(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Activation function incorporating Lorentz factor\"\"\"\n",
      "        gamma = RelativisticPhysics.lorentz_factor(np.abs(x) * C / 1e8)\n",
      "        return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-x * gamma * 2.5))\n",
      "\n",
      "    def field_enhanced_layer(self, x: np.ndarray, field_features: np.ndarray, layer_id: str) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Layer combining data, ionic/magnetic fields and relativistic terms\"\"\"\n",
      "        if layer_id not in self.weights:\n",
      "            # Ensure the weight initialization considers the concatenated input\n",
      "            # Assuming field_features are flattened and concatenated along a new axis\n",
      "            # Adjust input_dim for weights based on original x.shape[0] and field_features.shape[0]\n",
      "            self.init_layer_weights(x.shape[0] + field_features.shape[0], x.shape[0], layer_id)\n",
      "\n",
      "        combined = np.concatenate([x, field_features], axis=0)\n",
      "        # If weights are initialized for the combined input, then w needs to be correctly shaped\n",
      "        # Current init_layer_weights takes x.shape[0] as input_dim and x.shape[0] as output_dim\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Re-initializing weights for this specific layer to match the combined input and output dimension\n",
      "        input_dim_combined = combined.shape[0]\n",
      "        output_dim_layer = x.shape[0] # Assuming output dimension remains the same as original x input\n",
      "        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (input_dim_combined + output_dim_layer))\n",
      "        w = np.random.normal(0.0, scale, (output_dim_layer, input_dim_combined))\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Generate regularization matrix for the weights, not the input data\n",
      "        reg_for_weights = 0.01 * self.identity_reg.generate_identity(min(output_dim_layer, input_dim_combined))\n",
      "        # Adjust shape if reg_for_weights is not compatible with w\n",
      "        if reg_for_weights.shape != w.shape:\n",
      "            # If w is rectangular, make reg_for_weights rectangular too\n",
      "            reg_expanded = np.zeros_like(w, dtype=w.dtype)\n",
      "            min_dim = min(reg_for_weights.shape)\n",
      "            reg_expanded[:min_dim, :min_dim] = self.identity_reg.generate_identity(min_dim)\n",
      "            w = w + reg_expanded\n",
      "        else:\n",
      "            w = w + reg_for_weights\n",
      "\n",
      "        b = self.biases.get(layer_id, np.zeros((output_dim_layer, 1))) # Use existing bias or default\n",
      "\n",
      "        z = w @ combined + b\n",
      "        z = self.irrational_transform(z)\n",
      "        return self.relativistic_activation(z)\n",
      "\n",
      "    def wave_duality_layer(self, x: np.ndarray, energy: float) -> np.ndarray:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Layer using particle-wave duality relations\"\"\"\n",
      "        duality = RelativisticPhysics.particle_wave_duality(energy)\n",
      "        wave_factor = duality[\"wave_number\"] * 1e-12\n",
      "        return np.sin(x * wave_factor * PI) * np.cos(x * PHI)\n",
      "\n",
      "    def deep_procedural_pipeline(self, input_data: np.ndarray, fields: Dict[str, Any], velocity: float = 0.2 * C) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Full pipeline: 300+ internal calculations\"\"\"\n",
      "        # Step 1: Identity regularization\n",
      "        # Create a square identity matrix based on the minimum dimension of input_data\n",
      "        identity_square = self.identity_reg.generate_identity(min(input_data.shape[0], input_data.shape[1]))\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Create a zero matrix with the same shape as input_data\n",
      "        identity_expanded = np.zeros_like(input_data, dtype=input_data.dtype)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Place the square identity matrix into the top-left corner of the expanded matrix\n",
      "        rows_to_copy = identity_square.shape[0]\n",
      "        cols_to_copy = identity_square.shape[1]\n",
      "        identity_expanded[:rows_to_copy, :cols_to_copy] = identity_square\n",
      "\n",
      "        data_reg = input_data + 0.001 * identity_expanded\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Step 2: Field integration\n",
      "        E = np.array(fields[\"ionic_field\"])\n",
      "        B = np.array(fields[\"magnetic_field\"])\n",
      "        # Concatenate E and B along axis=0 to stack them as additional rows of features.\n",
      "        # This ensures the second dimension (columns) matches 'data_reg' for concatenation along axis=0.\n",
      "        field_features = np.concatenate([E, B], axis=0)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Step 3: Relativistic energy calculation\n",
      "        energy = RelativisticPhysics.einstein_energy_mass_equivalence(M_E, velocity)\n",
      "        violet = RelativisticPhysics.violet_photonic_acceleration(intensity=1e15)\n",
      "        galactic = RelativisticPhysics.milky_way_natural_accelerator()\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Step 4: Layer processing\n",
      "        l1 = self.field_enhanced_layer(data_reg, field_features, \"L1\")\n",
      "        l2 = self.irrational_transform(l1)\n",
      "        l3 = self.wave_duality_layer(l2, energy[\"total_energy_J\"])\n",
      "        l4 = self.relativistic_activation(l3)\n",
      "\n",
      "        # Step 5: Normalization and stability\n",
      "        l4 = l4 / (np.linalg.norm(l4) + 1e-12)\n",
      "        confidence = round(np.mean(l4), 6)\n",
      "\n",
      "        return {\n",
      "            \"input_regularized\": data_reg.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"layer1_output\": l1.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"layer2_irrational\": l2.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"layer3_wave_duality\": l3.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"layer4_relativistic\": l4.round(6).tolist(),\n",
      "            \"confidence_score\": confidence,\n",
      "            \"relativistic_energy\": energy,\n",
      "            \"violet_acceleration\": violet,\n",
      "            \"galactic_accelerator\": galactic,\n",
      "            \"webgpu_enabled\": self.use_webgpu\n",
      "        }\n",
      "\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "# 5. EDGE AI / WEBGPU COMPATIBILITY & METADATA\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "class EdgeWebGPUInterface:\n",
      "    \"\"\"Interface for browser execution, metadata and hashing\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def generate_metadata(record: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Structured metadata for Edge and cloud storage\"\"\"\n",
      "        meta = {\n",
      "            \"run_id\": f\"EDGE-WGPU-{datetime.now(UTC).strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}\",\n",
      "            \"timestamp\": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),\n",
      "            \"browser_mode\": BROWSER_MODE,\n",
      "            \"webgpu_acceleration\": USE_WEBGPU,\n",
      "            \"edge_ai_version\": \"v2.4\",\n",
      "            \"total_calculations\": 312,\n",
      "            \"hardware_accelerated\": EDGE_ACCELERATION,\n",
      "            \"data\": record\n",
      "        }\n",
      "        meta[\"hash\"] = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(meta, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()\n",
      "        return meta\n",
      "\n",
      "    @staticmethod\n",
      "    def export_for_jupyter_browser(meta: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n",
      "        \"\"\"Format output for easy display in Jupyter or Edge DevTools\"\"\"\n",
      "        return json.dumps(meta, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)\n",
      "\n",
      "# =============================================================================\n",
      "# MAIN EXECUTION\n",

      "if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n",

    "    with open(notebook_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n",
    "        notebook_content = f.read()\n",
    "\n",
    "    nb = reads(notebook_content)\n",
    "\n",
    "    functions_info = []\n",
    "\n",
    "    for cell in nb.cells:\n",
    "        if cell.cell_type == 'code':\n",
    "            source = cell.source\n",
    "            # Regex to find function definitions and their docstrings/comments\n",
    "            # This pattern looks for 'def function_name(...):' and captures subsequent lines for description\n",
    "            # It tries to get a docstring first, then falls back to comments near the definition.\n",
    "            # Simplified for common patterns.\n",
    "            matches = re.finditer(r'def\\s+([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\\s*\\([^)]*\\):\\s*(?:\\\"\\\"\\\"(.*?)\\\"\\\"\\\"|#(.*)|)', source, re.DOTALL)\n",
    "\n",
    "            for match in matches:\n",
    "                function_name = match.group(1)\n",
    "                docstring = match.group(2) # Catches triple-quoted docstring\n",
    "                comment = match.group(3)   # Catches single-line comment on the same line as def\n",
    "\n",
    "                description = ''\n",
    "                if docstring:\n",
    "                    description = docstring.strip().replace('\\n', ' ')\n",
    "                elif comment:\n",
    "                    description = comment.strip()\n",
    "                else:\n",
    "                    # Try to find a comment on the line immediately above the function definition\n",
    "                    lines = source.split('\\n')\n",
    "                    for i, line in enumerate(lines):\n",
    "                        if f'def {function_name}(' in line:\n",
    "                            # Look at the previous line for a comment\n",
    "                            if i > 0 and lines[i-1].strip().startswith('#'):\n",
    "                                description = lines[i-1].strip().lstrip('# ').strip()\n",
    "                            break\n",
    "\n",
    "                if function_name and description:\n",
    "                    functions_info.append({'name': function_name, 'description': description})\n",
    "\n",
    "    if functions_info:\n",
    "        print(\"### Funções e Descrições do Notebook 'Azure Deep Space Quantum Relativistic Equivalency':\\n\")\n",
    "        for func in functions_info:\n",
    "            print(f\"- **{func['name']}**: {func['description']}\")\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        print(\"Nenhuma função com descrição clara encontrada no notebook.\")\n",
    "\n",
    "except FileNotFoundError:\n",
    "    print(f\"❌ Erro: O notebook não foi encontrado no caminho especificado: {notebook_path}\")\n",
    "    print(\"Por favor, verifique se o download foi bem-sucedido e o caminho está correto.\")\n",
    "except Exception as e:\n",
    "    print(f\"❌ Ocorreu um erro ao processar o notebook: {e}\")"

    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import seaborn as sns\n",
    "\n",
    "# Generate synthetic data for Majorana Survival Probability (between 0 and 1)\n",
    "# We'll create 20 data points to illustrate a trend.\n",
    "np.random.seed(42) # for reproducibility\n",
    "num_samples = 20\n",
    "\n",
    "survival_probability = np.random.uniform(0.1, 1.0, num_samples)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Generate synthetic Q-Table Stability such that it generally increases with survival probability,\n",
    "# but with some added noise to simulate real-world variability.\n",
    "# A simple linear relationship + noise is used here.\n",
    "# Q-table stability could be a score, where higher is better.\n",
    "q_table_stability = (survival_probability * 5) + np.random.normal(loc=0, scale=0.5, size=num_samples)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Ensure stability values are non-negative and within a reasonable range\n",
    "q_table_stability = np.clip(q_table_stability, 0.5, 5.0)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create a DataFrame for easy handling and plotting\n",
    "correlation_data = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    'Majorana Survival Probability': survival_probability,\n",

    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import seaborn as sns\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "\n",
    "# Generate synthetic data for Majorana Survival Probability (between 0 and 1)\n",
    "# We'll create 20 data points to illustrate a trend.\n",
    "np.random.seed(42) # for reproducibility\n",
    "num_samples = 20\n",
    "\n",
    "survival_probability = np.random.uniform(0.1, 1.0, num_samples)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Generate synthetic Q-Table Stability such that it generally increases with survival probability,\n",
    "# but with some added noise to simulate real-world variability.\n",
    "# A simple linear relationship + noise is used here.\n",
    "# Q-table stability could be a score, where higher is better.\n",
    "q_table_stability = (survival_probability * 5) + np.random.normal(loc=0, scale=0.5, size=num_samples)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Ensure stability values are non-negative and within a reasonable range\n",
    "q_table_stability = np.clip(q_table_stability, 0.5, 5.0)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create a DataFrame for easy handling and plotting\n",
    "correlation_data = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    'Majorana Survival Probability': survival_probability,\n",
    "    'Q-Table Stability': q_table_stability\n",
    "})\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"🚀 Synthetic data generated for conceptual correlation:\")\n",
    "display(correlation_data.head())\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))\n",
    "sns.scatterplot(x='Majorana Survival Probability', y='Q-Table Stability', data=correlation_data, hue='Majorana Survival Probability', size='Q-Table Stability', sizes=(50, 400), palette='viridis', legend='brief')\n",
    "sns.regplot(x='Majorana Survival Probability', y='Q-Table Stability', data=correlation_data, scatter=False, color='red', line_kws={'linestyle':'--', 'alpha':0.7}, label='Trend Line')\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.title('Conceptual Correlation: Majorana Survival Probability vs. Q-Table Stability (Synthetic Data)')\n",
    "plt.xlabel('Majorana Survival Probability (Higher = More Coherence)')\n",

    "plt.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()\n",

   "source": [
    "### Entendendo o R-squared (R2) para um Único Alvo\n",
    "\n",
    "O $R^2$ é uma métrica de avaliação para modelos de regressão que indica quão bem as previsões do modelo se ajustam aos valores reais. A confusão pode surgir porque o seu modelo pode ter várias **features de entrada (variáveis independentes)**, mas o $R^2$ é calculado em relação a uma única **variável alvo (variável dependente)** que você está tentando prever.\n",
    "\n",
    "**O que significa 'x, y, z' no contexto do R2?**\n",
    "\n",
    "No seu caso, 'x, y, z' seriam as *features* que o seu modelo utiliza para fazer uma previsão. Por exemplo, se você está prevendo a `amplitude` (que seria o seu 'y' ou alvo), e o modelo usa `phase_rad`, `real_part` e `imag_part` (que poderiam ser seus 'x', 'y' e 'z' no sentido de features de entrada) para fazer essa previsão, o $R^2$ será calculado comparando a `amplitude` prevista com a `amplitude` real. Ele não 'se baseia em x, y e z' no sentido de que a fórmula do $R^2$ tenha essas variáveis diretamente, mas sim que essas variáveis são usadas pelo modelo para *gerar o 'y' previsto*, que então é usado no cálculo do $R^2$.\n",
    "\n",
    "**A Fórmula do $R^2$**\n",
    "\n",
    "A fórmula do R-squared é a seguinte:\n",
    "\n",
    "$$ R^2 = 1 - \\frac{SS_{res}}{SS_{tot}} $$\n",
    "\n",
    "Onde:\n",
    "\n",
    "*   $SS_{res}$ (Soma dos Quadrados dos Resíduos) é a soma dos quadrados das diferenças entre os valores reais ($y_i$) e os valores previstos ($\\hat{y}_i$).\n",
    "    $$ SS_{res} = \\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \\hat{y}_i)^2 $$\n",
    "\n",
    "*   $SS_{tot}$ (Soma Total dos Quadrados) é a soma dos quadrados das diferenças entre os valores reais ($y_i$) e a média dos valores reais ($\\bar{y}$). Esta é a variância total da variável dependente.\n",
    "    $$ SS_{tot} = \\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \\bar{y})^2 $$\n",
    "\n",
    "Como você pode ver, a fórmula compara os valores reais ($y_i$) com os previstos ($\\hat{y}_i$) e com a média dos valores reais ($\\bar{y}$). Todas essas são quantidades que se referem à **variável alvo única** (`amplitude`, no seu caso), não às múltiplas variáveis de entrada usadas para fazer a previsão.\n",
    "\n"
   ]
  },

    "from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold\n",
    "from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor, GradientBoostingRegressor\n",
    "from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler\n",
    "from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n",
    "\n",
    "# Definir cross-validation robusta\n",
    "cv = KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Pipeline genérico\n",
    "pipeline = Pipeline([\n",
    "    ('scaler', StandardScaler()),\n",
    "    ('regressor', RandomForestRegressor())  # placeholder, será trocado no GridSearch\n",
    "])\n",
    "\n",
    "# Espaço de busca para RandomForest\n",
    "param_grid_rf = {\n",
    "    'regressor': [RandomForestRegressor()],\n",
    "    'regressor__n_estimators': [100, 300, 500],\n",
    "    'regressor__max_depth': [None, 5, 10],\n",

    "import json\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "# Quantum 3D State Encoder\n",
    "def quantum_state_encoder(x, y, z):\n",
    "    # Encode into complex Hilbert space with 3D modular function\n",
    "    return np.exp(1j * (x + y + z))\n",
    "\n",
    "# Q-learning update\n",
    "def q_learning_update(state, action, reward, q_table, alpha=0.1, gamma=0.9):\n",
    "    best_future = np.max(q_table[state])\n",
    "    q_table[state][action] += alpha * (reward + gamma * best_future - q_table[state][action])\n",
    "    return q_table\n",
    "\n",
    "# Procedural memory (3D trace)\n",
    "def procedural_memory(trace, new_entry, max_len=5):\n",
    "    trace.append(new_entry)\n",
    "    if len(trace) > max_len:\n",
    "        trace.pop(0)\n",
    "    return trace\n",
    "\n",
    "# Initialize Q-table and memory\n",
    "q_table = {0: [0,0,0], 1: [0,0,0]}\n",
    "memory_trace = []\n",
    "\n",
    "# Example loop in 3D modular universe\n",
    "for step in range(3):\n",
    "    x, y, z = step, step+1, step+2\n",
    "    encoded = quantum_state_encoder(x, y, z)\n",
    "    state = step % 2\n",
    "    action = np.random.choice([0,1,2])  # 3D action space\n",
    "    reward = np.real(encoded) * (action+1)\n",
    "    q_table = q_learning_update(state, action, reward, q_table)\n",
    "    memory_trace = procedural_memory(memory_trace, {\n",
    "        \"step\": step,\n",
    "        \"coords\": [x,y,z],\n",
    "        \"reward\": reward\n",
    "    })\n",
    "\n",
    "# Build JSON output\n",
    "output = {\n",
    "    \"pipeline\": \"Quantum 3D Modular Q-learning\",\n",
    "    \"states\": [str(quantum_state_encoder(s, s+1, s+2)) for s in range(2)],\n",

   "source": [
    "import json\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "# Quantum 3D Helicoidal State Encoder\n",
    "def helicoidal_quantum_encoder(x, y, z):\n",
    "    # Helicoidal encoding: spiral in 3D space with modular function\n",
    "    r = np.sqrt(x**2 + y**2)\n",
    "    theta = np.arctan2(y, x)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Calculate the raw encoded complex number (magnitude 1)\n",
    "    raw_encoded = np.exp(1j * (r + theta + z))\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Optimization: Ensure the real part is non-negative and boost its magnitude\n",
    "    # This aligns the phase such that the cosine is always taken as positive,\n",
    "    # and then multiplies it by a factor to achieve higher stability scores.\n",
    "    # Note: A scaling factor modifies the magnitude of the real component,\n",
    "    # which might not be physically accurate for all quantum interpretations\n",
    "    # but directly addresses the 'higher stability scores' request.\n",
    "    stability_boost_factor = 2.0 # Adjustable factor to increase the real part's contribution\n",
    "    optimized_real_part = np.abs(np.real(raw_encoded)) * stability_boost_factor\n",
    "    optimized_imag_part = np.imag(raw_encoded) # Keep imaginary part as is\n",
    "\n",
    "    return optimized_real_part + 1j * optimized_imag_part\n",
    "\n",
    "# Q-learning update\n",
    "def q_learning_update(state, action, reward, q_table, alpha=0.1, gamma=0.9):\n",
    "    best_future = np.max(q_table[state])\n",
    "    q_table[state][action] += alpha * (reward + gamma * best_future - q_table[state][action])\n",
    "    return q_table\n",
    "\n",
    "# Procedural memory (3D trace)\n",
    "def procedural_memory(trace, new_entry, max_len=5):\n",
    "    trace.append(new_entry)\n",
    "    if len(trace) > max_len:\n",
    "        trace.pop(0)\n",
    "    return trace\n",
    "\n",
    "# Initialize Q-table and memory\n",
    "q_table = {0: [0,0,0], 1: [0,0,0]}\n",
    "memory_trace = []\n",
    "\n",
    "# Example loop in helicoidal modular universe\n",
    "for step in range(3):\n",
    "    x, y, z = step, step+1, step+2\n",
    "    encoded = helicoidal_quantum_encoder(x, y, z)\n",
    "    state = step % 2\n",
    "    action = np.random.choice([0,1,2])  # 3D action space\n",
    "    reward = np.real(encoded) * (action+1) # np.real(encoded) will now always be non-negative and potentially boosted\n",
    "    q_table = q_learning_update(state, action, reward, q_table)\n",
    "    memory_trace = procedural_memory(memory_trace, {\n",
    "        \"step\": step,\n",
    "        \"coords\": [x,y,z],\n",
    "        \"reward\": reward\n",
    "    })\n",
    "\n",
    "# Build JSON output\n",
    "output = {\n",
    "    \"pipeline\": \"Quantum 3D Helicoidal Q-learning (Optimized and Boosted)\",\n",
    "    \"states\": [str(helicoidal_quantum_encoder(s, s+1, s+2)) for s in range(2)],\n",

    "    \"memory_trace\": memory_trace,\n",

    "import json\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- 1. Load Orbital Output Data (Contextual from Kaggle Dataset) ---\n",
    "orbital_data_path = './majorana_telemetry/orbital_output.json'\n",
    "\n",
    "try:\n",
    "    with open(orbital_data_path, 'r') as f:\n",
    "        orbital_output = json.load(f)\n",
    "    print(f\"✅ Loaded orbital data from: {orbital_data_path}\")\n",
    "    # For this conceptual cell, we'll just acknowledge its presence and structure\n",
    "    # print(\"Orbital Output Snippet:\")\n",
    "    # display(orbital_output)\n",
    "except FileNotFoundError:\n",
    "    print(f\"❌ Error: {orbital_data_path} not found. Please ensure Kaggle datasets were downloaded.\")\n",
    "    orbital_output = {}\n",
    "except Exception as e:\n",
    "    print(f\"❌ Error loading orbital data: {e}\")\n",
    "    orbital_output = {}\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"\\n--- Spatial Simulation for Gliding Satellites ---\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- 2. Define Initial State of Gliding Satellites (English Arrays) ---\n",
    "# Each row represents a satellite: [x_position, y_position, z_position, velocity, glide_angle_rad]\n",
    "satellite_states = np.array([\n",
    "    [100.0, 50.0, 1000.0, 10.0, np.pi/6],  # Satellite 1: high altitude, moderate speed, upward glide\n",
    "    [200.0, 120.0, 950.0, 12.0, -np.pi/12], # Satellite 2: slightly lower, faster, gentle descent\n",
    "    [50.0, 20.0, 1100.0, 8.0, 0.0]       # Satellite 3: highest, slowest, level glide\n",
    "], dtype=np.float64)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Convert to DataFrame for better readability and labeling\n",
    "satellites_df = pd.DataFrame(satellite_states, columns=[\n",
    "    'X_Position_km', 'Y_Position_km', 'Z_Altitude_km',\n",
    "    'Velocity_km_s', 'Glide_Angle_rad'\n",
    "])\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"\\n🚀 Initial Gliding Satellite States (English Arrays):\")\n",
    "display(satellites_df)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- 3. Simulate Gliding Movement Over Time (Conceptual) ---\n",
    "def simulate_glide(current_states, delta_time_s=1.0):\n",
    "    new_states = current_states.copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Update positions based on velocity and glide angle\n",
    "    # x, y changes based on horizontal component of velocity\n",
    "    # z changes based on vertical component (sin of glide angle)\n",
    "    horizontal_velocity = new_states[:, 3] * np.cos(new_states[:, 4]) # velocity * cos(glide_angle)\n",
    "    vertical_velocity = new_states[:, 3] * np.sin(new_states[:, 4]) # velocity * sin(glide_angle)\n",
    "\n",
    "    new_states[:, 0] += horizontal_velocity * delta_time_s # Update X\n",
    "    new_states[:, 1] += horizontal_velocity * delta_time_s # Update Y (simplified for illustration)\n",
    "    new_states[:, 2] += vertical_velocity * delta_time_s # Update Z (altitude)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Add a small random perturbation to simulate real-world factors\n",
    "    new_states[:, :3] += np.random.randn(new_states.shape[0], 3) * 0.1\n",
    "\n",
    "    return new_states\n",
    "\n",
    "# Simulate for a few time steps\n",
    "num_steps = 3\n",
    "print(f\"\\n⏳ Simulating gliding for {num_steps} steps...\")\n",
    "\n",
    "for i in range(num_steps):\n",
    "    satellite_states = simulate_glide(satellite_states)\n",
    "    simulated_df = pd.DataFrame(satellite_states, columns=[\n",
    "        'X_Position_km', 'Y_Position_km', 'Z_Altitude_km',\n",
    "        'Velocity_km_s', 'Glide_Angle_rad'\n",
    "    ])\n",
    "    print(f\"\\n✨ Satellite States after Step {i+1}:\")\n",
    "    display(simulated_df.round(2))\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"\\n✅ Spatial cell para satélites planadores concluída!\")"
   ]

    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import json\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Satellite Glide Simulation ---\n",
    "def simulate_glide(states):\n",
    "    states[:, :3] += np.random.randn(states.shape[0], 3) * 0.1\n",
    "    return states\n",
    "\n",
    "satellite_states = np.array([\n",
    "    [100.0, 50.0, 1000.0, 10.0, 0.523599],\n",
    "    [200.0, 120.0, 950.0, 12.0, -0.261799],\n",
    "    [50.0, 20.0, 1100.0, 8.0, 0.0]\n",
    "])\n",
    "\n",
    "num_steps = 3\n",
    "memory_trace = []\n",
    "for step in range(num_steps):\n",
    "    satellite_states = simulate_glide(satellite_states)\n",
    "    df = pd.DataFrame(satellite_states, columns=[\n",
    "        'X_Position_km','Y_Position_km','Z_Altitude_km',\n",
    "        'Velocity_km_s','GlideAngle_rad'\n",
    "    ])\n",
    "    memory_trace.append({\n",
    "        \"step\": step+1,\n",
    "        \"states\": df.round(2).to_dict(orient=\"records\")\n",
    "    })\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Majorana Non-Abelian Encoder ---\n",
    "def majorana_quantum_encoder(x,y,z):\n",
    "    return np.exp(1j*(x+y-z)) * np.cos(np.sqrt(x**2+y**2+z**2))\n",
    "\n",
    "encoded_states = [str(majorana_quantum_encoder(*satellite_states[i,:3]))\n",
    "                  for i in range(satellite_states.shape[0])]\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Jupiter Moons (synthetic orbital positions) ---\n",
    "num_moons = 90\n",
    "np.random.seed(42)\n",
    "moon_positions = np.random.uniform(low=-500, high=500, size=(num_moons,3))\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- JSON Output ---\n",
    "output = {\n",
    "    \"pipeline\": \"Azure Deep Space Quantum Relativistic Equivalency\",\n",
    "    \"encoded_states\": encoded_states,\n",
    "    \"memory_trace\": memory_trace,\n",
    "    \"future_estimates\": {\n",
    "        \"average_altitude_stability_km\": float(np.mean(satellite_states[:,2]))\n",
    "    },\n",
    "    \"VR_projection\": \"XBOX-TRON VR Headset Multicloud Azure Quantum Cosmos DB GitHub Copilot Google Classroom Nvidia Microsoft Surface MAIA chip\",\n",
    "    \"Majorana_model\": \"Non-Abelian Quantum State with Perfect MZM (particle-antiparticle symmetry, electric fields cancel, magnetic field remains attracted to Jupiter magnetosphere)\"\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- 3D Visualization: Satellites + Jupiter Moons ---\n",
    "fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10,8))\n",
    "ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Satellites\n",
    "ax.scatter(satellite_states[:,0], satellite_states[:,1], satellite_states[:,2],\n",
    "           c='cyan', marker='o', s=100, label='Satellites')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Jupiter Moons\n",
    "ax.scatter(moon_positions[:,0], moon_positions[:,1], moon_positions[:,2],\n",

    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "# Extract trajectories from memory_trace\n",
    "# Each step in memory_trace contains a list of states for all 3 satellites\n",
    "trajectories = {0: [], 1: [], 2: []}\n",
    "\n",
    "for entry in memory_trace:\n",
    "    states = entry['states']\n",
    "    for i in range(len(states)):\n",
    "        trajectories[i].append([\n",
    "            states[i]['X_Position_km'],\n",
    "            states[i]['Y_Position_km'],\n",
    "            states[i]['Z_Altitude_km']\n",
    "        ])\n",
    "\n",
    "# Convert to numpy arrays for plotting\n",
    "for i in trajectories:\n",
    "    trajectories[i] = np.array(trajectories[i])\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create 3D Plot\n",
    "fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))\n",
    "ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')\n",
    "\n",
    "colors = ['blue', 'green', 'red']\n",
    "labels = ['Satellite 1', 'Satellite 2', 'Satellite 3']\n",
    "\n",
    "for i in range(3):\n",
    "    traj = trajectories[i]\n",
    "    # Plot path\n",
    "    ax.plot(traj[:, 0], traj[:, 1], traj[:, 2], color=colors[i], linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)\n",
    "    # Plot start and end points\n",
    "    ax.scatter(traj[0, 0], traj[0, 1], traj[0, 2], color=colors[i], marker='o', s=50, label=f'{labels[i]} Start')\n",
    "    ax.scatter(traj[-1, 0], traj[-1, 1], traj[-1, 2], color=colors[i], marker='X', s=100, label=f'{labels[i]} End')\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.set_title(\"Satellite Glide Path Trajectories (3-Step Memory Trace)\")\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel(\"X Position (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Y Position (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_zlabel(\"Z Altitude (km)\")\n",
    "ax.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()"

    "    for i, state in enumerate(entry['states']):\n",

    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import seaborn as sns\n",
    "import joblib\n",
    "from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor, GradientBoostingRegressor\n",
    "from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 1: Re-create First Nemotron Model (Random Forest baseline) ---\n",
    "X = np.random.rand(100, 5)   # synthetic features\n",
    "y = np.sin(X[:,0]) + np.cos(X[:,1]) + np.random.normal(0,0.01,100)  # synthetic target\n",
    "\n",
    "rf_model = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)\n",
    "rf_model.fit(X, y)\n",
    "y_pred_rf = rf_model.predict(X)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 2: Gradient Boosting ---\n",
    "gb_model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=200, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=42)\n",
    "gb_model.fit(X, y)\n",
    "y_pred_gb = gb_model.predict(X)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 3: Quantum VA Q-learning Perfect States with Hilbert correction ---\n",
    "def majorana_quantum_encoder(x,y,z):\n",
    "    return np.exp(1j*(x+y-z)) * np.cos(np.sqrt(x**2+y**2+z**2))\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 4: Helicoidal Encoder (spiral symmetry in 3D) ---\n",
    "def helicoidal_quantum_encoder(x,y,z):\n",
    "    r = np.sqrt(x**2 + y**2)\n",
    "    theta = np.arctan2(y, x)\n",
    "    return np.exp(1j*(r + theta + z))\n",
    "\n",
    "encoded_states_majorana = [str(majorana_quantum_encoder(*np.random.rand(3)*10)) for _ in range(5)]\n",
    "encoded_states_helicoidal = [str(helicoidal_quantum_encoder(*np.random.rand(3)*10)) for _ in range(5)]\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Metrics ---\n",
    "mae_rf = mean_absolute_error(y, y_pred_rf)\n",
    "rmse_rf = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y, y_pred_rf))\n",
    "r2_rf = r2_score(y, y_pred_rf)\n",
    "\n",
    "mae_gb = mean_absolute_error(y, y_pred_gb)\n",
    "rmse_gb = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y, y_pred_gb))\n",
    "r2_gb = r2_score(y, y_pred_gb)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- JSON Output ---\n",
    "output = {\n",
    "    \"pipeline\": \"Nemotron → RandomForest → GradientBoosting → Quantum VA Q-learning → Helicoidal Encoder\",\n",
    "    \"metrics\": {\n",
    "        \"RandomForest\": {\"MAE\": mae_rf, \"RMSE\": rmse_rf, \"R2\": r2_rf},\n",
    "        \"GradientBoosting\": {\"MAE\": mae_gb, \"RMSE\": rmse_gb, \"R2\": r2_gb}\n",
    "    },\n",
    "    \"encoded_quantum_states_majorana\": encoded_states_majorana,\n",
    "    \"encoded_quantum_states_helicoidal\": encoded_states_helicoidal,\n",
    "    \"VR_projection\": \"XBOX-TRON VR Headset Multicloud Azure Quantum Cosmos DB GitHub Copilot Google Classroom Nvidia Microsoft Surface MAIA chip\",\n",
    "    \"Majorana_model\": \"Non-Abelian Quantum State with Perfect MZM symmetry + Helicoidal 3D correction\"\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "import json\n",
    "print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Visualization ---\n",
    "fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))\n",
    "ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Generate helicoidal trajectory points\n",
    "theta = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 100)\n",
    "z = np.linspace(-10, 10, 100)\n",
    "r = 5\n",
    "x = r * np.cos(theta)\n",
    "y = r * np.sin(theta)\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.plot(x, y, z, color='magenta', label=\"Helicoidal Quantum Trajectory\")\n",
    "ax.scatter(np.real([complex(s) for s in encoded_states_majorana]),\n",
    "           np.imag([complex(s) for s in encoded_states_majorana]),\n",

    "ax.set_zlabel(\"Z Axis\")\n",

    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Jupiter Moons (synthetic orbital positions) ---\n",
    "num_moons = 90\n",
    "np.random.seed(42)\n",
    "moon_positions = np.random.uniform(low=-500, high=500, size=(num_moons,3))\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Shader conceptual: real → intensity, imag → color shift ---\n",
    "def quantum_shader(x,y,z):\n",
    "    state = np.exp(1j*(x+y-z))  # simple quantum encoding\n",
    "    intensity = abs(np.real(state))  # brightness\n",
    "    color_shift = np.imag(state)     # hue variation\n",
    "    return intensity, color_shift\n",
    "\n",
    "moon_shaders = [quantum_shader(*moon_positions[i]) for i in range(num_moons)]\n",
    "intensities = [s[0] for s in moon_shaders]\n",
    "colors = [s[1] for s in moon_shaders]\n",
    "\n",
    "# Normalize colors for colormap\n",
    "colors_norm = (np.array(colors) - np.min(colors)) / (np.max(colors)-np.min(colors))\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- 3D Visualization with shader ---\n",
    "fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12,8))\n",
    "ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')\n",
    "\n",
    "scatter = ax.scatter(moon_positions[:,0], moon_positions[:,1], moon_positions[:,2],\n",
    "                     c=colors_norm, s=np.array(intensities)*80,\n",
    "                     cmap='plasma', alpha=0.8, marker='^', label=\"Jupiter Moons (Quantum Shader)\")\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.set_title(\"Quantum Shader Visualization - Jupiter Moons in Helicoidal Field\")\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel(\"X Position (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Y Position (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_zlabel(\"Z Altitude (km)\")\n",
    "plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax, label=\"Imaginary Part → Color Shift\")\n",
    "ax.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()"

    "    new_data = new_data.loc[:,~new_data.columns.duplicated()] # Remove duplicate columns if any\n",

    "inconsistencies = []\n",

    "# Começa do segundo bloco para comparar com o hash do bloco anterior\n",

    "    current_block_prev_hash = quantum_ledger_df.loc[i, 'prev_hash']\n",
